paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Rebekah overheard Isaac's plan to bless Esau, and she came to Jacob with a plan of her own (Genesis 27:5-10). It had a disguise, a dish and a lie, and Jacob said "I am Esau, your firstborn" (Genesis 27:19). The passage shows us a deception that works in the moment and is still called what it is: Isaac said Jacob "came deceitfully" (Genesis 27:35).

And look at what it cost. Right after Jacob left his father's presence, Esau returned from the hunt (Genesis 27:30). Isaac "began to tremble violently" (Genesis 27:33), and Esau "let out a loud and bitter cry" (Genesis 27:34). I think this is the heavy part of the lesson: a plan can get a blessing spoken over you and still leave a family hurting.

Now hold on, because the story isn't over. Isaac told Esau, "But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck" (Genesis 27:40), so the last word on this family hasn't been spoken. I'm not going to tell you what comes next, baker. I'll just say that when your plan needs goat skin on your neck (Genesis 27:16), that's your sign to stop and think.
